title: Naan
description: Soft, pillowy leavened flatbread traditionally cooked in a tandoor — this stovetop version gets a similar char using a hot cast-iron tawa.
steps: Dissolve the sugar and yeast in the lukewarm water and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
In a large bowl, mix the flour and salt. Add the curd, oil and the yeast mixture, and knead into a soft, slightly sticky dough for 8-10 minutes.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, until roughly doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide into 6-8 equal balls. Roll each into an oval or teardrop shape, about a quarter-inch thick.
Heat a heavy tawa over high heat. Wet one side of the rolled naan lightly with water and press the wet side onto the hot tawa — it should stick.

Cover with a lid and cook until bubbles form and the base is lightly charred, 1-2 minutes. Then hold the tawa upside down directly over a flame for a few seconds to char the top, or finish under a hot grill.
Brush with butter and garnish with coriander leaves if using. Repeat with the remaining dough, serving each naan hot.
